queries.prompt: I want artists to build effects by dragging boxes onto a canvas and connecting their inputs and outputs with wires instead of writing code. How should I structure the thing they're editing
queries.rationale: core: visual node-based authoring, graph as data with nodes/pins/wires -> node-model.md

queries.prompt: each box has little sockets on the left and right and I need to stop people from plugging a color output into a number input. What's the right way to validate a connection as they draw it
queries.rationale: typed pins, connection validity checked at author time -> typing-and-connections.md

queries.prompt: my editor graph is getting walked from scratch every frame and it's slow; I'd rather turn the authored graph into some flat ordered thing once and just run that
queries.rationale: compile/lower to flattened executable form vs interpret editor graph -> evaluation-and-compilation.md

queries.prompt: some nodes do expensive image filtering and I don't want to recompute them when nothing upstream changed. How do I know a node's result is still valid
queries.rationale: validity-hash caching from node settings + input hashes -> evaluation-and-compilation.md

queries.prompt: I want to select a cluster of nodes and collapse them into a single reusable box that I can drop into other graphs, with named inputs and outputs
queries.rationale: subgraph encapsulation behind a typed interface, create-from-selection -> subgraphs-and-functions.md

queries.prompt: how do I run a graph that contains other graphs nested inside it without my evaluator having to understand the nesting: can I just inline them before running
queries.rationale: flatten/inline subgraphs at compile, evaluator sees flat DAG -> subgraphs-and-functions.md

queries.prompt: one input on a node should just use a typed-in default value when there's no wire plugged into it, so I don't need a separate constant node for every literal
queries.rationale: unwired input falls back to stored constant default -> authoring-and-introspection.md

queries.prompt: we want plugins to be able to register brand new box types and new kinds of data that can travel on the wires without touching the core editor
queries.rationale: data-driven node-type + wire-type registry extensible by plugins -> authoring-and-introspection.md / node-model.md

queries.prompt: one node should adapt its input and output types depending on what's wired into it: a CPU image vs a GPU image, instead of me making two near-identical nodes
queries.rationale: polymorphic/variant node resolving pin types from connections -> typing-and-connections.md

queries.prompt: the last node in my graph produces a draw call but nothing actually runs it; where is the work supposed to get scheduled from
queries.rationale: terminal/output node hands result to owning system which schedules -> node-model.md (scheduling itself -> designing-gpu-renderers)

queries.prompt: should one graph output just a single texture, or should I bundle the mesh, material, and textures of a whole object into one big graph. What does that decide for my project
queries.rationale: asset granularity fine vs uber-graph, sets project data layout -> authoring-and-introspection.md

queries.prompt: artists can't tell why the final output looks wrong because they can't see the data coming out of any of the intermediate boxes. How do I let them inspect a wire
queries.rationale: per-pin introspection / preview of intermediate values -> authoring-and-introspection.md

queries.prompt: when I disconnect and reconnect a wire the types of a flexible node go stale and validation lies; when should I re-resolve and re-check
queries.rationale: re-resolve polymorphic pins + re-validate on every connect/disconnect -> typing-and-connections.md

queries.prompt: I need to schedule a frame of render passes with the right barriers and layout transitions across an explicit GPU API
queries.rationale: near-miss: GPU render/frame graph scheduling and barriers -> designing-gpu-renderers, not authoring node graphs

queries.prompt: how should I lay out a big array of components in struct-of-arrays so iterating them is cache-friendly
queries.rationale: near-miss: CPU data-oriented memory layout -> applying-data-oriented-design, not node-graph design

queries.prompt: I'm designing the reflectable typed object store with properties and references that everything serializes into
queries.rationale: near-miss: the underlying typed data model / object store -> designing-data-models, not the graph layer on top

queries.prompt: I'm building the core document store for our level editor: objects of different kinds each with a set of named properties, and I want to add new object types at runtime without recompiling. How should the type/property schema work?
queries.rationale: near miss owned by designing-data-models

queries.prompt: our particle simulator stalls when we have 50k particles. The update loop reads position and velocity out of a fat 96-byte struct, can you restructure it for cache efficiency
queries.rationale: near miss owned by applying-data-oriented-design

queries.prompt: our renderer hand-writes a barrier before and after every pass and it breaks every time we reorder passes. I want passes to just declare what they read and write and have ordering and transitions figured out for us
queries.rationale: near miss owned by designing-gpu-renderers

queries.prompt: our editor lets artists drop in an FBX or PNG and we want them edited in-tool but shipped as packed GPU-ready data. How should we structure the two forms so editing and loading don't fight each other
queries.rationale: near miss owned by designing-asset-pipelines

queries.prompt: give me a single typed object database where every node has properties, children it owns, and links to other nodes by id, and the whole thing notifies on edit, supports undo, and saves to a versioned file
queries.rationale: near miss owned by designing-data-models

queries.prompt: we need to emit different compressed texture formats and byte order per target platform but share one source asset. How should the pipeline handle platforms
queries.rationale: validation near miss owned by designing-asset-pipelines
